item.research_question: How can a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film with superior mechanical and tribological properties be synthesized using a cost-effective single consolidated target, and what are the effects of annealing on its adhesion and wear resistance?
item.material_system: Equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates
item.processing_route: DC-magnetron sputtering using a single target prepared by partial spark plasma sintering (SPS) of equimolar elemental powders (Cu, Mo, Ta, W, V) at 1000 °C under 40 MPa pressure; film deposition at 500 °C substrate temperature for 120 min; annealing at 300 °C for adhesion improvement
item.test_conditions: Nanoindentation at 3 mN load; nanopillar compression (440 nm diameter) with max force 3 mN; tribological wear tests at room temperature (RT) and 300 °C using 1 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed against E52100 alloy steel counterballs
key_findings: The as-deposited film exhibited a nanocrystalline body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with an average grain size of 18 nm and a thickness of ~900 nm.
Nanoindentation yielded an average hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.
Nanopillar compression tests revealed a high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa (yield strength 10.7 ± 0.8 GPa).
Annealing at 300 °C reduced surface roughness to 2 nm (Sa) and significantly improved film adhesion compared to the as-deposited state.
The annealed film showed an average coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.25 at RT and 1.5 at 300 °C.
Wear rates were 6.4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N m at RT and 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N m at 300 °C, which are 10² times lower than 304 stainless steel at RT.
The film hardness was ~20% higher than previously reported RHEA films in the literature.
item.mechanism: The high hardness and strength are attributed to nanocrystalline grain size, grain boundary strengthening, solid solution hardening, lattice distortion, and sluggish diffusion. The strengthening mechanism in nanopillars shifts from dislocation-controlled to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation, leading to intergranular fracture. Annealing improves adhesion and stability, while the formation of CuO at 300 °C influences tribological behavior.
item.limitations: The as-deposited film showed excessive plastic deformation, smearing, and radial cracks due to low adhesion, leading to a sharp increase in COF after 15 m of sliding. The film composition showed in-depth nonhomogeneity, being rich in W, Ta, and Mo at the surface and V at the interface. The high COF at 300 °C was attributed to tribochemical reactions and oxide formation on the counterball.
item.future_work: The study suggests that RHEA films can be beneficial for wear and nanopillar applications and may lead to processing for large-scale industrial applications.
quotes: The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.
A high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa was obtained in nanopillar compression due to solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.
The COF was found to be 2 times lower at RT and wear rate 102 times lower at RT and 300 °C than those of 304 stainless steel.
